judged_text: Salesforce eager refresh on every instantiation plus fragile status check: a Salesforce token refresh (network call + credential DB write) now runs on every service instantiation where previously jsforce used the stored access token and refreshed lazily, adding a per-operation round trip (a downed/rate-limiting Salesforce now fails operations that previously succeeded with the cached token); the fetch has no timeout, and the guard response.statusText !== "OK" is fragile since HTTP/2 responses carry an empty reason phrase, with the response body discarded on failure so the thrown HttpError says only "Bad Request" with no diagnostic detail (salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:~75-98)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new logic unconditionally performs a token refresh via `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then writes the refreshed token back to Prisma (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, meaning every call to this auth/connection setup now incurs a network round-trip + DB write. Additionally, the failure guard `if (response.statusText !== "OK")` is fragile (it should use `response.ok`/`response.status`), and on failure it discards the response body and throws an `HttpError` with only `statusText` (and a hardcoded `statusCode: 400`), reducing correctness/diagnostic quality. No timeout/abort is used for the `fetch`, so the request can hang indefinitely.
